correctness.rationale: For an idempotent endomorphism, if a maps to an outside element A=a^u b then A=f(A)=A^u f(b), making f(b) commute with the order-four A, which contradicts inversion. If b maps inside the cyclic subgroup, a maps to 1 or a^m. The first case is trivial by idempotence; the second requires m odd by idempotence but then a^m is not a square inside the cyclic subgroup. In the remaining normal form the relations require c odd and idempotence gives c²=c, cv=0 mod 2m. CRT gives the claimed active coordinates and the forced two-primary residue. The image meets the cyclic subgroup in a cyclic subgroup of order 2d_S and has one further coset. Checking composition on b shows that two maps commute exactly when their shared inactive labels agree. This gives the all-arity product including t=0, and the binomial transform for the trivial map. In the reduced graph, the two single-inactive-coordinate intermediates on distinct coordinates give distance at most three, and two all-inactive vectors disagreeing at every coordinate have no common reduced neighbor. For k=0 and k=1 this gives the empty and edgeless cases respectively. Complete label vectors give exactly the maximal cliques, and coordinate counting gives the degrees. For m=15 the pair count is 1+48+160=209.

originality.rationale: The central all-arity compatibility law and reduced clique model have exact mathematical coverage via a distinct general affine-retraction result on odd generalized dihedral groups. Let n be the odd part of m and N=<a^n> have order 2^(e+1). The quotient is Dih(C_n). Each nontrivial dicyclic retraction fixes N pointwise and induces the cyclic affine pair (P,u) on the quotient, where P is multiplication by c mod n and u=v mod n. Conversely each quotient pair with P²=P and P(u)=0 has exactly one such lift by imposing c=1 and v=0 on the two-primary coordinate. The correspondence preserves composition and includes the trivial map separately, so tuple and graph claims transfer, not merely numerical coincidences. The scaled image orders and the diameter observation do not furnish a surviving substantive distinct compatibility theorem. This is a coverage decision, not a priority or copying judgment: the distinct records are indexed on the same UTC date.
residual_risks: Chronological priority of the same-day records is unresolved; Theorem 6.1 primary text could not be accessed. Neither issue weakens the demonstrated mathematical equivalence. No priority judgment is made.
